lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: distance-preserving versus non-distance-preserving transformations

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Rotate the point (-7, 11) counterclockwise about the origin by 90°. Give the image.
A regular polygon has 9 sides. How many rotations about its centre, strictly between 0° and 360°, carry it onto itself, and what is the smallest such angle?

Triangle ABC has vertices A(-2, 4) and B(4, 2). After a transformation the images are A′(2, -4) and B′(-4, -2), and the triangle keeps its size and orientation sense. Which single rigid motion describes this?
Point P(5, -2) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 9, y + 1). Give the image P′.
Reflect the point (11, 2) across the y-axis. Give the image.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: Rotate the point (2, 11) counterclockwise about the origin by 270°. Give the image.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A regular polygon has 8 sides. How many rotations about its centre, strictly between 0° and 360°, carry it onto itself, and what is the smallest such angle?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has vertices A(-8, -9) and B(-9, 8). After a transformation the images are A′(8, 9) and B′(9, -8), and the triangle keeps its size and orientation sense. Which single rigid motion describes this?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
